title: Heap buffer overflow in `_format_TracebackException` when `TracebackException.format` omits newline
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in a 1-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
allocator_layer: libc malloc (the object never reaches a pymalloc pool)
layer_note: measured: ASan reported a 1-byte region, at or under the 512 B SMALL_REQUEST_THRESHOLD

spatial.oracle: a fault at the offending access: cause 5 on a load or 7 on a store where the access leaves the object's own capability, or cause 24 where it reaches memory the system allocator has already freed and revoked. The object is a system allocator block, so one of the two applies; completion would falsify this.

sublet.oracle: fault: the object is a libc malloc block

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the arm does not separate this case, and the admissible outcomes are stated rather than one of them predicted: si_code=1 (PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS) where the access goes beyond the bounds the allocator actually set, si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) where it instead lands in memory a revocation sweep has already reclaimed, or completion where it stays inside the bounds the allocator set -- malloc may bound a capability to a rounded size class rather than the requested length. The mechanism is live and the run proves it rather than assuming it: mech-control S_OOB faults with si_code=1. Any other si_code would falsify this.

status: three arms measured 2026-10-06: cheri11, spatial-20261006-105111, sublet-20261006-112658
